# FLX-3504: a sink was given a target or an option it cannot use

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

A sink writes only where it is told to and only in ways it can name, so it checks its target and its options before it opens: a file sink needs a directory that is not a file, a stream whose expose id is a safe single path segment, and options of the right type and range; every sink needs to be opened on the stream it was set up for. A target written as a URL must be an object store URL (s3://, gs://, az:// or abfs://); file://, memory://, ftp:// and any other scheme are refused, and a local directory is written as a plain path. An ADBC uri that holds a secret inline is refused as well, in any form: a password in user information (user:PW@host, with or without a scheme), a pair named like a credential (sig, token, password, access_token, X-Amz-Signature) in a query split on ?, & or ;, in a fragment, in a libpq key=value string (the value may be quoted) or in an ODBC Key=Value; string (PWD, Password). Put the uri in an environment variable and pass --sink-opt uri-env=NAME. The object store tuning options (request-timeout, connect-timeout, max-retries, retry-timeout) must be whole numbers in their range, and are refused for a local directory. The message names the target or the option and says what it expects. Nothing was written, and no run was started.

## Look it up offline

```console
$ fluxsim explain FLX-3504
```
